title: Hosted API Meter Definitions (v3) — Canonical Dictionary + Edge Cases
author: Wei Chen
body:
## Purpose
This page is the **single source of truth** for how Redwood Inference measures usage for the **Hosted API**. It defines:
- Meter names and units (tokens, requests, embedding units, rerank units)
- Which events are billable vs non-billable
- Streaming accounting and disconnect handling
- Rounding / aggregation rules used for invoicing
- Versioning expectations and compatibility notes

This document is intended for Finance, RevOps/Sales Ops, Support, Product, and Engineering. If a customer dispute arises, Support should follow the runbook and reference **these definitions**.

---

## Scope
**In-scope endpoints (Hosted API):**
- Chat/completions (streaming and non-streaming)
- Embeddings
- Rerank

**Out of scope:** Dedicated/Private contract attribution, revenue recognition policy, and plan pricing details. This page defines **measurement**, not price.

---

## Canonical sources (systems of record)
All billed quantities must be explainable from raw telemetry.

### Telemetry (raw)
- Dataset: `telemetry.llm_request_events_v2` (event-level)
- Primary keys (conceptual): `request_id`, `attempt_id`, `event_time`
- Required dimensions (must exist for billable events):
  - `account_id`, `workspace_id`
  - `api_key_id` (nullable for some enterprise auth flows)
  - `model_id` (resolved model), `model_alias` (customer-facing name)
  - `region`
  - `endpoint_type` (chat|completions|embeddings|rerank)
  - `request_outcome` (see below)
  - `retry_reason` (nullable)

### Billing aggregates (invoice-ready)
- Dataset: `billing.hosted_api_usage_agg_v3` (daily aggregates)
- Produced by: metering pipeline (owner: **Nadia Rahman**) + billing hooks (owner: **Cole Summers**)
- Contracted invoice window (default): calendar month, **UTC**

### Console usage (customer-facing)
- Dataset/view: `console.usage_hosted_api_v3`
- Must match billing aggregates for the same time window and dimensions (allowing for presentation rounding only).

---

## Key terms
### Token
A **token** is the atomic unit produced by the tokenizer associated with the serving model family.
- For metering, we count tokens as the model runtime reports them for the request/attempt.
- Token counts are always **integers** at the event level.

### Request vs Attempt
- **Request**: a customer-initiated API call (identified by `request_id`).
- **Attempt**: an execution attempt of that request (identified by `attempt_id`). Retries create additional attempts.

### Billable event
A telemetry event that is included in invoice aggregation according to the billability rules below.

---

## Meter catalog (v3)
The Hosted API uses the following canonical meters. Each meter is reported as a **raw quantity** and later mapped to invoice line items/prices.

| Meter key (canonical) | Unit | Applies to | Definition (high level) |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `input_tokens` | tokens | chat/completions | Tokens in the customer prompt/messages actually processed for the winning attempt |
| `output_tokens` | tokens | chat/completions | Tokens generated and delivered (or recorded as delivered) for the winning attempt |
| `cached_input_tokens` | tokens | chat/completions | Subset of input tokens served from prefix/KV cache (informational; pricing treatment depends on plan/experiment) |
| `requests` | requests | all | Count of billable requests (1 per request_id) |
| `embedding_input_tokens` | tokens | embeddings | Tokens in the input text(s) embedded |
| `embedding_requests` | requests | embeddings | Billable embedding requests (1 per request_id) |
| `rerank_units` | units | rerank | Total candidate documents scored (sum of `top_k`/`documents_count` per request) |
| `rerank_requests` | requests | rerank | Billable rerank requests (1 per request_id) |

Notes:
- `cached_input_tokens` is a **sub-meter** of `input_tokens` (i.e., `cached_input_tokens <= input_tokens`).
- `requests` is a cross-endpoint meter, but invoices commonly split requests by endpoint family or omit request-based line items depending on plan.

---

## Billability rules (Hosted API)
Billability is determined at the request level and then applied to token/unit meters.

### Request outcomes (v3)
Telemetry sets `request_outcome` to one of:
- `success` — request completed successfully (non-streaming) or stream completed normally
- `partial_success_client_disconnect` — stream started and client disconnected mid-stream (billable for delivered portion)
- `rejected_customer_error` — invalid request (4xx), auth failure, quota exceeded, etc. (not billable)
- `failed_server_error` — 5xx before any billable usage is produced (not billable)
- `failed_after_partial_output` — server error after some output was produced (billable for produced portion; rare)

**Canonical billability logic:**
- Billable if `request_outcome IN (success, partial_success_client_disconnect, failed_after_partial_output)`.
- Not billable if `request_outcome IN (rejected_customer_error, failed_server_error)`.

### Retries
Retries can occur due to transient infrastructure issues or upstream provider failures (where applicable).
- Only the **winning attempt** contributes tokens/units to billable meters.
- Non-winning attempts must be excluded even if they produced tokens.
- `retry_reason` is used for debugging and reconciliation (e.g., `capacity_failover`, `upstream_timeout`, `worker_evicted`).

Operational note: If you see “double counting,” the first check is whether aggregation incorrectly included multiple attempts per `request_id`.

---

## Meter definitions (precise)
This section provides the precise definitions used by `billing.hosted_api_usage_agg_v3`.

### 1) `input_tokens` (chat/completions)
**Definition:**
- `input_tokens` = tokens in the request prompt/messages **processed by the runtime** for the winning attempt.

**Telemetry fields (winning attempt):**
- `prompt_tokens` (int)
- `cached_prompt_tokens` (int, may be 0)

**Computation:**
- `input_tokens = prompt_tokens`
- `cached_input_tokens = cached_prompt_tokens`

**Constraints:**
- `0 <= cached_input_tokens <= input_tokens`

**Edge cases:**
- Tool/function calling: tool schemas included in the prompt count toward `input_tokens` if they are part of the messages sent to the model.
- Server-side prompt assembly (e.g., system policy injections): if injected tokens are part of the actual model prompt, they are included in `prompt_tokens`. (This is rare for Hosted API; any material change requires Legal + Finance sign-off.)

### 2) `output_tokens` (chat/completions)
**Definition:**
- `output_tokens` = tokens generated by the model and **delivered to the client** for the winning attempt.

**Telemetry fields:**
- Non-streaming: `completion_tokens` (int)
- Streaming: `stream_emitted_tokens` (int)

**Computation:**
- If `streaming=false`: `output_tokens = completion_tokens`
- If `streaming=true`: `output_tokens = stream_emitted_tokens`

**Streaming note:** We intentionally use emitted/delivered tokens rather than “generated internally” tokens.

### 3) `requests` (all endpoints)
**Definition:**
- `requests` = count of billable requests.

**Computation:**
- `requests = COUNT(DISTINCT request_id)` filtered to billable outcomes.

**Important:** Requests are not multiplied by retries. Retries exist at the attempt level.

### 4) `embedding_input_tokens` and `embedding_requests`
**Definition:**
- `embedding_input_tokens` = tokens of all embedding inputs in the request.
- `embedding_requests` = count of billable embedding requests.

**Telemetry fields:**
- `embedding_prompt_tokens_total` (int) — sum over all inputs
- `inputs_count` (int)

**Computation:**
- `embedding_input_tokens = embedding_prompt_tokens_total`
- `embedding_requests = COUNT(DISTINCT request_id)` filtered to billable outcomes

**Edge cases:**
- Multi-input embeddings are supported; token count must be the sum across inputs.
- Empty strings: treated as customer error and should be `rejected_customer_error` (not billable).

### 5) `rerank_units` and `rerank_requests`
**Definition:**
- `rerank_units` = total number of candidate documents scored.
- `rerank_requests` = count of billable rerank requests.

**Telemetry fields:**
- `documents_count` (int) — number of candidates scored

**Computation:**
- `rerank_units = SUM(documents_count)` over billable outcomes
- `rerank_requests = COUNT(DISTINCT request_id)` over billable outcomes

**Edge cases:**
- If the request specifies `top_k`, metering is based on **candidates scored**, not results returned.
- If an internal safety filter reduces returned results, metering is unchanged (still candidates scored).

---

## Streaming accounting (Hosted API)
Streaming is the most common source of customer confusion. These rules are aligned with **ADR-027**.

### What we bill for streaming
For streaming responses we bill:
- All `input_tokens` for the winning attempt (prompt was processed)
- Only `output_tokens` that were **emitted/delivered** before termination

### Client disconnects
If the client disconnects:
- Outcome: `partial_success_client_disconnect`
- `output_tokens` includes only tokens emitted before disconnect.
- Tokens generated after disconnect must not be billed.

### Server errors mid-stream
If the server fails after emitting some tokens:
- Outcome: `failed_after_partial_output`
- Bill the emitted portion (`output_tokens = stream_emitted_tokens`).

### Common mismatch causes (streaming)
If a customer reports “console tokens differ from invoice,” check:
1. Time window (console time zone vs invoice UTC month)
2. Whether the customer is comparing “generated tokens” vs “emitted tokens”
3. Retries (multiple attempts; only winning attempt should count)
4. Backfills (rare; see meter versioning and invoice run notes)

---

## Caching and batching (Hosted API)
### Cached tokens
`cached_input_tokens` represent tokens served from prefix/KV cache.
- They are counted as part of `input_tokens`.
- Pricing treatment may vary by plan or experiment (e.g., discounted cached tokens). The meter definition does not change.

### Continuous batching
Continuous batching is a runtime optimization and must not change the logical meter definitions.
- Token counts are per-request, not per-batch.
- Any aggregation that accidentally applies batch-level counters to multiple requests is a defect and must be escalated.

---

## Aggregation windows and rounding
### Aggregation window
- Billing aggregation is daily in `billing.hosted_api_usage_agg_v3` using **UTC day boundaries**.
- Invoice aggregation is monthly using UTC month boundaries.

### Rounding policy (usage quantities)
Aligned to **ADR-027**:
- Token-based meters are stored as integers and **never rounded per request**.
- Unit conversions for pricing (e.g., “per 1K tokens”) are applied during invoice preparation.
- Invoice line item quantities may be represented with up to **6 decimal places** for unit quantities (e.g., kilo-tokens) to minimize rounding drift.

### Rounding policy (currency)
- Extended amounts are rounded to the invoice currency’s standard precision (typically 2 decimals).

### Display vs bill
- Console may display rounded quantities (e.g., 3 decimals for kilo-tokens). These are **presentation-only** and must reconcile to invoice totals when using the underlying unrounded aggregates.

---

## Required dimensions for reporting and invoicing
For each billable meter record, the following dimensions must be present in the billing aggregate:
- `account_id`
- `workspace_id`
- `model_id` (resolved)
- `model_alias` (customer-facing)
- `region`
- `endpoint_type`
- `meter_version`
- `aggregation_window_start_utc`, `aggregation_window_end_utc`

Recommended (used for experiments/segmentation):
- `customer_tier` (self_serve|growth|enterprise)
- `plan_id` / `pricing_experiment_variant` (if applicable)

If any required dimension is missing, it is considered a **meter health failure** and should trigger alerts (see anomaly dashboards).

---

## Versioning
### Meter version key
All Hosted API billing exports must include `meter_version`.
- Current version: **v3**

### What triggers a new meter version
A meter version bump is required when any of the following changes:
- Definition of billable outcomes
- Streaming emission accounting
- Inclusion/exclusion of cached tokens from any canonical meter
- Token source fields or dedupe logic that can change customer-visible quantities

### v3 changes (from v2)
- Removed per-request rounding in invoice aggregation path (aggregate raw integer tokens; apply conversion rounding at invoice stage).
- Standardized streaming `output_tokens` to emitted/delivered tokens and added explicit outcomes for client disconnect vs server failure.
- Introduced `request_outcome` and `retry_reason` dimensions to separate billable vs non-billable attempts and support reconciliation.

---

## Reconciliation expectations (sanity thresholds)
For reconciliation methodology and sampling, see the linked methodology page. At a high level:
- Target: billing aggregates reconcile to raw telemetry within **0.1%** at the account-month level for stable periods.
- Known acceptable variance categories (must be explainable):
  - Backfills rerunning a window (should converge post-backfill)
  - Late-arriving telemetry within the agreed ingestion SLA

Any unexplained variance > threshold should be treated as a defect or a missing dimension and escalated to Telemetry/Metering owners.

---

## FAQ (internal)
### Are “cached tokens” billed?
The meter is always recorded. Whether cached tokens are billed at the same rate, discounted, or free is **pricing**, not measurement, and may vary by contract/experiment. Refer to invoice mapping and the customer’s order form.

### Do we bill for failed requests?
Not for `rejected_customer_error` or `failed_server_error`. If partial output was emitted (streaming) we bill only the emitted portion.

### Why do some customers see invoice > console?
Most commonly: comparing different time zones/windows, or comparing rounded console displays to unrounded invoice quantities. Secondary causes include retries (attempt vs request) and historical backfills.
